note: Minimal record for the existing procedure.kings-court reference, from data/laws/SOURCES.md sections westminster-2-1285-c1-de-donis, treason-1351. This shared court reference is not a uniform trial procedure. De donis names the king's courts and says heirs with a reversion who are of full age, in England and free need not make a claim. For treason the king's judges hear cases, an overt act is proved (the courts' reading), and a doubtful unlisted case waits for parliament and the king to decide whether it is treason or felony. These law-specific statements do not supply a common presiding officer, judge, initiation, proof or appeal rule; those fields remain null.
